 Live .  92,888 viewing 92888 viewing Live page Updated 1 minute ago Antonelli becomes youngest world champion in history as Verstappen wins in Mexico
 Mexican Grand Prix
 BBC Radio 5 Live
 Close Mexican Grand Prix
 BBC Radio 5 Live
 Listen live Live Reporting (active) 
 Leaderboard 
 Summary
 Antonelli is world champion as Verstappen wins Mexico City Grand Prix
 Italian Antonelli, 20, becomes youngest title winner in F1 history
 Mercedes driver finished third in Mexico, with Hamilton second after battle with Ferrari team-mate Leclerc
 Benson Q&A: Send us your questions 
 Close form Send us your F1 views
 Get involved Live Reporting
 Lorraine McKenna
 Post published at 22:24 GMT 22:24 GMT 
 Damon Hill 
1996 world champion on BBC Radio 5 Live in Mexico City 
 Lewis is just not giving Max a moment's peace, he is just on his tail the whole time. Kimi is just watching these two masters fight it out at the front. 
 250 31 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Norris challenging Leclerc published at 22:24 GMT 22:24 GMT 
 Lap 70/71 
 It's so close to overtake for Lando Norris! Time is running out for the world champion but Charles Leclerc is defending for his life in the Ferrari. He keeps hold of fourth place, Norris will probably have to settle for fifth. 
 28 13 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 22:22 GMT 22:22 GMT 
 Lap 69/71 
 I think Kimi Antonelli will be happy to be on the podium with two multiple world champions to celebrate his maiden title victory. 
 Charles Leclerc is surviving on track right now. Lando Norris hasn't found the answer just yet, and he's only got a few laps to figure it out. 
 382 38 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 22:21 GMT 22:21 GMT 
 Lap 68/71 
 Polesitter Lewis Hamilton in second continues to be the fastest car on the Mexican circuit, but he hasn't got enough boost in the Scuderia to mount a challenge for the lead. 
 Max Verstappen is sixth tenths clear of the seven-tine world champion, with Italian Kimi Antonelli in the final podium place in third. 
 429 109 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 22:19 GMT 22:19 GMT 
 Lap 67/71 
 The long sprint to Turn One doesn't present Lando Norris with an opportunity to pass Charles Leclerc. Maybe try again at Turn Four? Denied. The Ferrari stays ahead in P4. 
 Max Verstappen is on his way to another victory this season, as Kimi Antonelli is inching closer to becoming the youngest title winner in Formula 1 history. 
 361 135 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 22:18 GMT 22:18 GMT 
 Damon Hill 
1996 world champion on BBC Radio 5 Live in Mexico City 
 There is another looming dilemma for Kimi Antonelli. He is actually very close to Lewis Hamilton and I wonder if he is thinking, I can have him. Because if he does think that, he shouldn't and I'm sure his engineers would say no, no Kimi just don't get involved in this one.
 516 81 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 22:18 GMT 22:18 GMT 
 Lap 66/71 
 The laps are ticking down but Lando Norris hasn't solved the puzzle of how to pass Charles Leclerc. The Ferrari driver is doing everything he can to keep the McLaren at arm's length. 
 118 89 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 22:17 GMT 22:17 GMT 
 Lap 65/71 
 That incident between Arvid Lindblad and Oscar Piastri at the restart is going to be investigated by the stewards. The Racing Bulls driver is out of this race, while Australian Piastri is still in th points in seventh. 
 145 52 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 get involved Get Involved published at 22:16 GMT 22:16 GMT 
 Select the 'Get Involved' button to have your say 
 Please can someone give a shout out to Lawson?! He's now in 10th and in the points after starting in the pits! What a drive!
 Victoria, Newark 
 789 90 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 22:16 GMT 22:16 GMT 
 Lap 64/71 
 Image source, Getty Images The Alpines of Pierre Gasly and Franco Colapinto are on to score points for the French team while Liam Lawson, who started in the pit lane, will collect points for fifth-placed Racing Bulls. 
 Max Verstappen leads from Lewis Hamilton, with Kimi Antonelli so close to his title party. 
 253 34 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 22:14 GMT 22:14 GMT 
 Lap 63/71 
 If Charles Leclerc thought the latest restart we hand him a break, he was wrong. Lando Norris is all over the back of his Ferrari but yet again, he lives to fight another lap in fourth. 
 286 107 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Safety car ending published at 22:13 GMT 22:13 GMT 
 Lap 62/71 
 Please, Mexico, no more drama - we need to go to bed. 
 Max Verstappen lets loose and sprints off at the restart. Lewis Hamilton is thinking about a move, but he doesn't have enough in the tank to make the lunge. 
 352 178 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Team radio - Piastri to McLaren published at 22:12 GMT 22:12 GMT 
 Piastri: "Is it a little bit of damage or a lot of damage?"
 Mclaren: "It's a reasonable amount of damage, Oscar."
 137 99 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Team radio - Leclerc to Ferrari published at 22:11 GMT 22:11 GMT 
 Leclerc: "I think I'm seeing the cord of the tyre."
 379 76 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 22:11 GMT 22:11 GMT 
 Damon Hill 
1996 world champion on BBC Radio 5 Live in Mexico City 
 Now typically, safety car restart doesn't really do much, you think it might be an opportunity but by the time they finish the start-finish line everyone is up to speed.
 133 35 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Safety car published at 22:11 GMT 22:11 GMT 
 Lap 61/71 
 Oscar Piastri asks his engineer how the bad the damage is to his car following that contact with Arvid Lindblad at Turn One. "Is it a lot?" says the Australian. "Reasonable amount," is the reply. 
 86 50 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Safety car published at 22:09 GMT 22:09 GMT 
 Lap 60/71 
 Image source, Getty Images The medical car is deployed with Arvid Lindblad in the barriers, but the British rookie tells his pit wall he's OK, and now he's safely out of the stricken Racing Bulls. 
 The safety car comes out with Max Verstappen leading from Lewis Hamilton and soon-to-be champion Kimi Antonelli. 
 301 80 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Team radio - McLaren to Norris published at 22:07 GMT 22:07 GMT 
 Engineer: "In our photos, Leclerc has a flat spot down to the canvas."
 Norris: "Yeah, I know that. I saw it."
 384 65 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 22:07 GMT 22:07 GMT 
 Lap 59/71 
 There seems to be a car stranded somewhere on track - it's rookie Arvid Lindblad, who has had a tangle with the McLaren of Oscar Piastri, and has been sent onto the grass and into the barriers. 
 82 162 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 22:06 GMT 22:06 GMT 
 Marc Priestley 
Former F1 mechanic on Radio 5 Live in Mexico City 
 I think when we get to the end of the race, we will hear from two McLaren drivers who spent almost all of it, incredibly frustrated because both of them have sat right behind the cars that they are chasing but just unable to get by them.
